note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment planning following recent biopsy results and rising PSA trajectory.

This 65-year-old office administrator presents for re-evaluation of his prostate cancer status. He was initially diagnosed with ISUP grade group 2 adenocarcinoma in August 2023, and a subsequent biopsy in January 2025 revealed ISUP grade group 1 disease with a cribriform pattern. His PSA has risen steadily from 1.5 ng/mL in August 2022 to 5.2 ng/mL currently. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 15. He is divorced and lives with his partner, who is his primary contact. He cycles approximately 20 km twice weekly and consumes 3 units of alcohol per week. He has a history of osteoarthritis and is currently under evaluation at the sleep clinic for suspected obstructive sleep apnoea. He expresses significant anxiety regarding invasive procedures and requests thorough discussion of all options.

On DRE, the prostate is smooth, symmetrical, and non-tender, consistent with a clinical T1c stage. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with stable vital signs, blood pressure 121/66 mmHg, and heart rate 65 bpm. No palpable lymphadenopathy or bone tenderness is noted.
